title: Thermal In Motion: Designing Thermal Flow Illusions with Tactile and Thermal Interaction
authors: Singhal, Yatharth; Honrales, Daniel; Wang, Haokun; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal motion, flowing thermal sensation, thermal referral, warm, cool, hot, cold
emotionAffectMeasurement: No direct emotion scale; focused on thermal motion perception and interviews.
thermalAffectJustification: Primarily empirical, focused on immersion rather than formal affect theory.
thermalCuePurpose: Create a perceived moving thermal cue for more immersive VR interaction.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Relative -15C to +9C from neutral skin temperature
temporalParameters: Warm-up around 1-3s, motion durations up to 10s
technicalSummary: Peltier and vibration were combined to produce a thermal motion illusion.
studyMethods: Multiple psychophysical user studies and qualitative interviews
contributions: Introduces thermal motion and key parameters for generating it.
contributionsToDesign: Shows how synchronized thermo-tactile timing can improve perceived motion and immersion.

title: Designing Beyond Hot and Cold - Exploring Full-Body Heat Experiences in Sauna
authors: Moesgen, Tim; Gowrishankar, Ramyah; Xiao, Yu
emotionTheoriesUsage: No explicit emotion model; grounded in phenomenology and somaesthetics.
thermalAffectJustification: Mainly from prior empirical HCI and lived sauna experience.
thermalCuePurpose: Understand and articulate full-body heat experience.
temporalParameters: Two sittings of around 10 minutes each
otherNote: No wearable thermal actuator in this paper.
technicalSummary: An observational study of naturally occurring whole-body heat experience.
studyMethods: Phenomenological interviews, body map, and sensory elicitation artifacts
contributions: Expands language and dimensions for describing heat experience.
contributionsToDesign: Proposes design parameters such as motion, timbre, and distribution.

title: Enhancing Food Coldness Perception via Synchronous Posterior Neck Cold stimulus during Swallowing
authors: Komiya, Shin'ichi; Nitto, Ryota; Ban, Yuki; Warisawa, Shin'ichi
thermalVocabularyDescription: cold stimulus, cooling sensation, coldness perception, thermal feedback
emotionAffectMeasurement: No emotion metric; comfort and deliciousness were secondary outcomes.
thermalAffectJustification: Focus on sensory perception enhancement rather than affect.
thermalCuePurpose: Enhance perceived food coldness without changing food temperature.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Cooling around 2.5-3.0C below baseline skin in constant condition
technicalSummary: Posterior neck cooling synchronized with swallowing increased perceived coldness.
studyMethods: Within-subject experimental user study with paired comparisons
contributions: Demonstrates temporal synchronization as a critical parameter for cross-modal coldness enhancement.
contributionsToDesign: Provides timing guidance for thermal-food interaction design.

title: Thermal Masking: When the Illusion Takes Over the Real
authors: Wang, Haokun; Singhal, Yatharth; Gil, Hyunjae; Kim, Jin Ryong
thermalVocabularyDescription: thermal masking, thermal referral, thermal migration, thermal illusion
thermalCuePurpose: Investigate thermal masking and perceptual relocation of thermal sensation.
technicalSummary: Shows vibrotactile cues can mask and relocate perceived thermal sensation.
studyMethods: Three controlled user studies with repeated-measures psychophysical methods
contributions: Introduces thermal masking effects and engineering implications for thermal displays.
contributionsToDesign: Supports designing larger perceived thermal coverage with fewer thermal actuators.

title: Hydroptical Thermal Feedback: Spatial Thermal Feedback Using Visible Lights and Water
authors: Ichihashi, Sosuke; Inami, Masahiko; Ho, Hsin-Ni; Howell, Noura
thermalVocabularyDescription: hydroptical thermal feedback, apparent motion, perceived water temperature
thermalCuePurpose: Create spatial and moving thermal sensations in water without changing bulk water temperature.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Perceived around 28C to 38C depending on illuminance
temporalParameters: Stimulus durations around 1-5s and SOA around 200-1000ms
technicalSummary: Visible light in water produced local warming, thermal apparent motion, and temperature illusion.
contributions: Introduces hydroptical thermal feedback as a new interaction method.
contributionsToDesign: Provides design recommendations and trade-offs for light-water thermal interaction.

title: Augmented Breathing via Thermal Feedback in the Nose
authors: Brooks, Jas; Mazursky, Alex; Hixon, Janice; Lopes, Pedro
thermalCuePurpose: Alter perceived airflow and breathing ease via synchronized intranasal heating/cooling.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Offsets around -10.5C to +10.6C from baseline intranasal temperature
technicalSummary: Intranasal thermal stimulation changed perceived breathing resistance without mechanical obstruction.
contributions: Demonstrates bidirectional perceived airflow modulation from thermal cues.
contributionsToDesign: Suggests thermal breathing feedback for VR, meditation, and assistive interactions.

title: ALCool: Utilizing Alcohol's Evaporative Cooling for Ubiquitous Cold Sensation Feedback
authors: Hamazaki, Takumi; Takami, Taiki; Ushiyama, Keigo; Mizoguchi, Izumi; Kajimoto, Hiroyuki
thermalCuePurpose: Provide low-power, long-duration cold sensation via alcohol evaporation and airflow.
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Cooling intensity depends on evaporation and fan speed
temporalParameters: 30s stimulation windows, effective cooling up to around 30-60 min per refill
technicalSummary: A wearable cooling system using alcohol evaporation achieved cold sensation with low power.
studyMethods: Two user studies plus technical evaluation
contributions: Presents a practical low-power alternative to Peltier-heavy cooling wearables.
contributionsToDesign: Supports ubiquitous cooling feedback and combined thermal-olfactory interaction design.
powerEnergyConsumption: Low power relative to Peltier baseline in the paper

title: Trigeminal-based Temperature Illusions
authors: Brooks, Jas; Nagels, Steven; Lopes, Pedro
thermalCuePurpose: Create warm/cool illusions via trigeminal scent stimulation without changing physical temperature.
mainActuatorModel: Piezo micro-pumps with vibrating mesh atomizer
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: Perceptual illusion, not direct temperature control
technicalSummary: Demonstrates temperature illusion in VR through trigeminal stimulation.
studyMethods: Two controlled studies (pairwise ratings and VR evaluation)
contributions: Introduces a low-power non-Peltier route for perceived thermal feedback.
contributionsToDesign: Shows trigeminal thermal illusion can shape perceived environmental temperature in VR.

title: The Impact of Thermal Cues on Affective Responses to Emotionally Resonant Vibrations
authors: Macdonald, Shaun Alexander; Pollick, Frank; Brewster, Stephen Anthony
emotionTheoriesUsage: Used as the analysis frame for valence and arousal responses.
emotionAffectMeasurement: Likert self-reports for valence, arousal, and emotional resonance.
thermalAffectJustification: Builds on prior thermotactile affect literature.
thermalCuePurpose: Test how thermal congruence modulates affective response to vibrotactile patterns.
technicalSummary: Combines thermal and vibrotactile cues to examine affective resonance changes.
contributions: Reports how thermal context shifts perceived emotional qualities of vibration.
contributionsToDesign: Guides thermo-vibrotactile composition for emotional interaction design.

title: Therminator: Understanding the Interdependency of Visual and On-Body Thermal Feedback in Virtual Reality
authors: Gunther, Sebastian; Muller, Florian; Schon, Dominik; Elmoghazy, Omar; Muhlhauser, Max; Schmitz, Martin
thermalCuePurpose: Study visual-thermal interdependency and perceived temperature realism in VR.
mainActuatorForTemperatureSensation: Water flow through PE-RT tube network
mainActuatorPossibleTemperatureRange: About 18C to 48C system range; tested 22.5C to 42.5C
temporalParameters: About 25s stimulation with around 12s full cold-to-hot transition capability
technicalSummary: A liquid-based on-body thermal display integrated with VR visuals.
contributions: Shows how visual context and thermal feedback jointly shape perception and comfort.
contributionsToDesign: Provides practical congruence guidance for thermal VR design.
